title: Je me lève, tu te lèves…
intro: A **reflexive verb** has an extra pronoun that refers back to the subject: *je **me** lève* (I get **myself** up). Most daily-routine verbs work this way. The verb itself is conjugated normally — you just add the right pronoun.

cases.label: me, te, se, nous, vous, se
cases.rule: Each subject has its own pronoun: *je **me** lève, tu **te** lèves, il **se** lève, nous **nous** levons, vous **vous** levez, ils **se** lèvent*.

cases.label: m', t', s' before a vowel
cases.rule: **me, te, se** become **m', t', s'** before a vowel or silent h: *je m'habille, tu t'appelles, il s'endort*.

cases.label: ne + pronoun + verb + pas
cases.rule: The pronoun stays glued to the verb: *je **ne me** lève **pas**, il **ne s'**habille **pas***.

cases.label: questions
cases.rule: Voice up, or **est-ce que**: *Tu te lèves ? Est-ce que tu te lèves ? À quelle heure tu te couches ?*

cases.label: after another verb: je vais me coucher
cases.rule: With an infinitive, the pronoun still matches the subject: *Je vais **me** coucher. Tu dois **te** lever. Nous allons **nous** reposer.*

cases.label: orders: lève-toi !
cases.rule: In orders, the pronoun goes after the verb with a hyphen, and **te → toi**: *Lève-toi ! Dépêche-toi ! Couchez-vous ! Reposons-nous !*

cases.label: je me lave / je lave la voiture
cases.rule: With **se**, you do it to yourself: *je me lave*. Without it, you do it to something or someone else: *je lave la voiture, je réveille Lou*.

cases.label: body parts: les, not mes
cases.rule: With a reflexive verb, body parts take **le / la / les**: *je me brosse **les** dents, elle se lave **les** mains* (not *mes dents*).

sections.title: 1. The reflexive pronouns
sections.tip: *nous nous* and *vous vous* look strange, but they're correct: the first is the subject, the second the reflexive pronoun.

sections.title: 2. Before a vowel: m', t', s'
sections.tip: You've known one since Unit 1: *je m'appelle* is a reflexive verb (*s'appeler*, literally “to call oneself”).

sections.title: 3. Saying no
text: **ne** comes before the pronoun, **pas** after the verb. The pronoun never leaves the verb.

examples.en: What time do you go to bed?

sections.title: 5. After another verb
text: After *aller, devoir, vouloir…* the reflexive verb is an infinitive — but its pronoun still matches the subject.

examples.en: I'm going to go to bed.

sections.title: 6. Orders: Lève-toi !
text: In a command, the pronoun comes **after** the verb with a hyphen, and **te** becomes **toi**.

sections.title: 7. Reflexive or not?
text: Many verbs exist both ways. With **se**, you do it to yourself. Without it, you do it to someone or something else.

sections.title: 8. Body parts: les, not mes
text: The reflexive pronoun already shows whose body it is, so French uses **le / la / les** — never *mon / ma / mes*.

mistakes.right: Je me lève à sept heures.
mistakes.why: *se lever* needs its pronoun: **je me lève**.
The pronoun matches the subject: **je … me**.
**me → m'** before a vowel or silent h.

story.title: Hugo, lève-toi !
story.en: Hugo's first morning at his new job doesn't start well.

lines.fr: Lundi matin, six heures. C'est le premier jour de travail de Hugo.
lines.en: Monday morning, six o'clock. It's Hugo's first day at work.

lines.fr: Le réveil sonne… mais Hugo {ne se réveille pas|refl-neg}.
lines.en: The alarm rings… but Hugo doesn't wake up.

lines.fr: Hmm… Quoi ? Quelle heure il est ?
lines.en: Hmm… What? What time is it?
Seven o'clock! Get up! Hurry up!

lines.fr: Oh non ! {Je me lève|refl-pronouns}, je me lève !
lines.en: Oh no! I'm getting up, I'm getting up!

lines.fr: Hugo {se douche|refl-pronouns} en deux minutes et {s'habille|refl-elision} très vite.
lines.en: Hugo showers in two minutes and gets dressed very quickly.

lines.fr: Où est ma brosse à dents ? {Je me brosse les dents|refl-body}…
lines.en: Where's my toothbrush? I'm brushing my teeth…

lines.fr: {Il se coiffe avec les mains|refl-body}, et il part.
lines.en: He does his hair with his hands, and leaves.

lines.fr: Hugo, {tu ne dois pas te coucher|refl-infinitive} si tard !
lines.en: Hugo, you mustn't go to bed so late!

lines.fr: Je sais… Ce soir, {je vais me coucher|refl-infinitive} à dix heures !
lines.en: I know… Tonight I'm going to bed at ten!

lines.fr: Dans la rue, il voit son voisin, {qui lave sa voiture|refl-vs-not}.
lines.en: In the street, he sees his neighbour, who is washing his car.

lines.fr: Bonjour, Hugo ! Vous êtes en retard ?
Oui ! Mon réveil {ne me réveille pas|refl-vs-not} !
lines.en: Yes! My alarm doesn't wake me up!

lines.fr: À huit heures et demie, Hugo arrive au bureau… avec une chaussette rouge et une chaussette bleue !
lines.en: At half past eight, Hugo arrives at the office… with one red sock and one blue sock!

quiz.en: What time do you go to bed?

quiz.q: How do you ask a friend “Are you getting up?”

quiz.en: I'm going to go to bed.
quiz.why: The pronoun matches the subject: **je … me**.
With reflexive verbs, body parts take **le / la / les**.
